name: Benign Keratosis
overview: Benign Keratosis-like Lesions (BKL), most commonly Seborrheic Keratoses, are among the most common benign skin growths. They are non-cancerous proliferations of epidermal cells and typically develop with increasing age. Although they do not become skin cancer, they may resemble malignant lesions such as melanoma or basal cell carcinoma, making clinical evaluation important when the diagnosis is uncertain.
description: Benign keratoses usually appear as well-defined lesions with a characteristic waxy or 'stuck-on' appearance. They may range in color from light tan to dark brown or black and often develop on the trunk, face, scalp, neck, or extremities. Lesions generally grow slowly over many years and are frequently discovered incidentally during routine skin examinations.
clinical_presentation: Flat, slightly raised, or elevated plaque
Usually multiple lesions in older adults
typical_features: Common on the chest, back, face, scalp, and shoulders
diagnostic_workup: Skin biopsy if diagnosis is uncertain or malignant features are suspected
treatment_options: No treatment required in most cases
Shave excision for symptomatic or cosmetically concerning lesions
prognosis: The prognosis is excellent. Benign keratoses are non-cancerous and do not metastasize. Most lesions remain stable or enlarge slowly over time. Treatment is generally performed only for cosmetic reasons, recurrent irritation, or diagnostic uncertainty.
prevention: Protect skin from excessive ultraviolet exposure
Attend routine dermatology examinations if numerous lesions are present
next_steps: Routine dermatological follow-up if recommended by your clinician.
No treatment is necessary unless the lesion becomes symptomatic or cosmetically bothersome.
Discuss removal options if irritation, recurrent trauma, or cosmetic concerns develop.
Seek medical evaluation if the lesion changes rapidly, develops irregular pigmentation, persistent bleeding, or ulceration.
red_flags: Development of features concerning for melanoma

follow_up.routine: Routine skin examinations as recommended by your healthcare provider.
follow_up.high_risk: Earlier review is appropriate if rapid changes or suspicious features develop.

patient_advice: Benign keratoses are common and usually harmless.
Avoid picking or scratching lesions to reduce irritation or bleeding.
Take periodic photographs to monitor for changes.
Seek medical evaluation if a lesion changes significantly in color, size, or shape.
Continue routine skin examinations, particularly if you have many pigmented lesions.
